## {#today .darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.todaymeta}
The full deck · four parts · every optional run in the main flow
:::

:::: {.todaybox}
::: {.nonincremental}
1. Credibility and tools – science, its crisis, and the toolchain
2. The claim and its estimand – the paper in full, estimands, and causal graphs
3. Reproduction and exploration – reproducing a published result, and working through the specification menu
4. Multiverse and preregistration – reading a specification curve, and declaring one analysis in advance
:::
::::

::: {.todaytake}
You leave with: a reproduced result · an estimand and a DAG of your own · a preregistered analysis · your dot on a live class multiverse
:::

::: {.todaymeta}
Work along in your IDE, solo or in pairs, with the browser lab page as the fallback
:::

::: notes
Welcome. This is the complete deck, and it includes all four of the optional runs of slides – the tools slides, the R tutorial, the methodological tutorial and the multiverse tutorial – that a one-day delivery can skip. That makes it longer than a single day can hold, so we take it over several sessions. The four parts follow one argument. The first asks why anyone thinks social science is in trouble, and what the tools have to do with it. The second goes inside one published paper and asks what question its claim actually answers. In the third you reproduce a recorded result and then vary it, and the fourth reads the spread of results that those variations produce before you declare the one analysis you would defend.
:::
